trap: 三字共用 -rogate（要求），差在字首；看到 -rogate 先看字首決定方向。

name: mendacious/mendicant

words.sent: The mendacious advertisement claimed the pills could cure every illness.
words.tr: 那則虛假的廣告宣稱這些藥丸能治百病。
words.src: Barron's U19；Hot Words L36；VA U17；字根字首 U200

words.sent: Medieval mendicant monks owned no property and depended on donations for food.
words.tr: 中世紀托缽修士不擁有財產，靠施捨維生。

tip_zh: mendacious 說謊的（mend 修補 → 編故事）；mendicant 乞討的（-cant 伸手 can't pay）
tip_en: mendacious = lying; mendicant = begging
trap: 開頭都是 mend-，學生容易以為兩字相關。

name: perspicacious/perspicuous

words.sent: A perspicacious investor, she sold her shares months before the market collapsed.
words.tr: 她是有洞察力的投資人，在市場崩盤前幾個月就賣掉持股。
words.src: Barron's U23；Hot Words L28；VA U35；字根字首 U57,135

words.def_: clearly expressed and easy to understand
words.sent: The manual's perspicuous instructions allowed even beginners to assemble the desk in minutes.
words.tr: 說明書的指示清楚易懂，連新手幾分鐘就能組好書桌。

tip_zh: perspicacious 人很敏銳（-acious 像 sagacious 有洞察力）；perspicuous 文字清楚易懂（-uous 像 conspicuous 顯而易見）
tip_en: perspicacious = insightful (person); perspicuous = clear (writing)
trap: 字根同為 spec（看），一個形容「看得透的人」，一個形容「讓人看得懂的文字」。

name: sententious/tendentious/pretentious

words.def_: given to moralizing in a pompous way
words.sent: The sententious speaker filled his talk with proverbs about hard work but offered no practical advice.
words.tr: 這位愛說教的講者滿口勤奮格言，卻沒提供任何實用建議。

words.def_: promoting a particular point of view; biased
words.sent: The documentary was criticized as tendentious because it interviewed only supporters of the policy.
words.tr: 這部紀錄片只訪問政策支持者，被批評立場偏頗。

words.def_: trying to seem more important or intelligent than one is
words.sent: The pretentious restaurant described its plain toast as "artisanal grain on a bed of dairy."
words.tr: 這家自命不凡的餐廳把普通吐司說成「乳製品襯底的職人穀物」。
words.src: Hot Words L3；字根字首 U60,138

tip_zh: sententious 愛說教（sentence 一句句格言）；tendentious 有偏見傾向（tend 傾向）；pretentious 自命不凡（pretend 假裝）
tip_en: sententious = preachy; tendentious = biased; pretentious = trying to seem important
trap: 兩字字尾相同，都帶貶義，但一個是「說教」，一個是「偏頗」。三字都是 -tentious 結尾：sententious 說教、tendentious 偏頗、pretentious 裝模作樣。

name: turbid/turgid/torpid

words.def_: cloudy or muddy, as with stirred sediment
words.sent: After the heavy rain, the river ran turbid and brown with soil from the hills.
words.tr: 大雨過後，河水因山上沖下的泥土而變得混濁發褐。

words.sent: Readers abandoned the turgid novel, whose every sentence was packed with needless adjectives.
words.tr: 讀者放棄了這本浮誇的小說，因為每句都塞滿多餘的形容詞。
words.src: Hot Words L2；字根字首 U230

words.sent: Snakes become torpid in cold weather and barely move until spring.
words.tr: 天冷時蛇會變得遲鈍，到春天前幾乎不動。
words.src: Hot Words L14；VA U37；字根字首 U229

tip_zh: turbid 混濁的（turbulent 攪動 → 水濁）；turgid 浮腫、文字浮誇（g = grand 誇大）；torpid 遲鈍、蟄伏（torpor 麻木）
tip_en: turbid = muddy; turgid = swollen, pompous; torpid = sluggish
trap: 只差 b／g；turbid 形容液體，turgid 形容腫脹或浮誇的文筆。三字都是 t-…-id 結構：turbid 混濁、turgid 腫脹浮誇、torpid 遲緩不動。

name: felicitous/solicitous

words.sent: Her felicitous choice of words eased the tension in the room.
words.tr: 她用字恰到好處，緩和了屋內的緊張氣氛。
words.src: Barron's U37；Hot Words L68；VA U40；字根字首 U184

words.sent: The solicitous nurse checked on the patient every hour through the night.
words.tr: 那位體貼的護理師整夜每小時都去探視病人。

tip_zh: felicitous 措辭恰當（felicity 幸福 → 剛剛好）；solicitous 關切殷勤（solicit 請求 → 熱心問候）
tip_en: felicitous = well-chosen; solicitous = caring, attentive
trap: 字尾相同、節奏相近；felicitous 形容用字，solicitous 形容對人的關心。

name: exculpate/inculpate/culpable/inculcate

words.sent: New DNA evidence exculpated the man, who had spent twelve years in prison.
words.tr: 新的 DNA 證據證明這名男子無罪，他已坐了十二年牢。

words.def_: to accuse or show to be guilty
words.sent: The emails inculpated the manager, revealing that he had approved the fraud.
words.tr: 這些電子郵件顯示經理批准了詐欺，讓他罪責難逃。

words.sent: The investigation found the driver culpable for the accident because he had been texting.
words.tr: 調查發現駕駛應為車禍負責，因為他當時在傳訊息。
words.src: Barron's U15；VA U31；字根字首 U176

words.def_: to teach an idea by repeating it often
words.sent: Parents try to inculcate good manners in their children from an early age.
words.tr: 父母從小就努力向孩子灌輸良好禮貌。

tip_zh: exculpate 開脫（ex- 移出 + culp 罪）；inculpate 歸罪（in- 放入罪）；culpable 有罪的（culp 罪）；inculcate 反覆灌輸（calc 踩 → 踩進腦中，與罪無關）
tip_en: exculpate = clear from blame; inculpate = blame; culpable = blameworthy; inculcate = teach by repetition
trap: 字根 culp（罪）相同，字首方向相反，學生常記反。inculcate 長得像 inculpate，卻和「罪」無關；culpable 則和 exculpate、inculpate 同字根。

name: impugn/impute/pugnacious

words.def_: to dispute the truth or honesty of
words.sent: The lawyer tried to impugn the witness's credibility by pointing out earlier lies.
words.tr: 律師指出證人先前說過謊，企圖質疑其可信度。
words.src: Hot Words L12；字根字首 U37

words.def_: to attribute a fault to someone
words.sent: It is unfair to impute the company's losses to a single employee.
words.tr: 把公司虧損歸咎於一名員工並不公平。

words.sent: The pugnacious senator seemed to enjoy picking fights with reporters.
words.tr: 那位好鬥的參議員似乎很喜歡和記者起衝突。
words.src: Barron's U4；Hot Words L7；VA U11；字根字首 U91,214

tip_zh: impugn 質疑抨擊（pugn 打 → 攻擊名譽）；impute 歸咎於（put 放到某人身上）；pugnacious 好鬥的（pugn 打，同 impugn）
tip_en: impugn = challenge as false; impute = attribute blame; pugnacious = eager to fight
trap: 兩字都是 imp- 開頭的指控動詞，差別在「攻擊真實性」與「把責任算到某人頭上」。pugnacious 和 impugn 同字根 pugn（打），一個是好鬥的性格，一個是攻擊對方的說法。

name: infamous/famous/infamy

words.sent: The prison was infamous for its harsh treatment of inmates.
words.tr: 這座監獄以虐待囚犯而惡名昭彰。

words.def_: known and recognized by many people
words.sent: The famous chef opened a small restaurant in her hometown.
words.tr: 這位知名主廚在家鄉開了一家小餐廳。

words.def_: the state of being well known for something bad
words.sent: The president called the surprise attack "a date which will live in infamy."
words.tr: 總統稱這場偷襲是「一個將永遠蒙羞的日子」。

tip_zh: in- 在這裡不是「不有名」，而是「壞名聲」→ 惡名昭彰；infamy 惡名（n.，infamous 的名詞）
tip_en: infamous = famous for bad reasons; infamy = bad reputation
trap: 學生以為 infamous = not famous（沒沒無聞），其實是「很有名，但是壞名聲」。infamy 和 infamous 一樣，in- 不是「沒有名氣」，而是「壞名聲」。

name: invaluable/worthless/valueless/priceless

words.sent: Her years of field experience proved invaluable when the team got lost in the mountains.
words.tr: 隊伍在山中迷路時，她多年的野外經驗變得無比珍貴。

words.sent: After the company went bankrupt, its shares became worthless.
words.tr: 公司破產後，股票變得一文不值。

words.sent: The old coins turned out to be valueless copies.
words.tr: 那些舊錢幣原來是不值錢的仿製品。

words.def_: so valuable that no price can be put on it
words.sent: The museum's most priceless treasure is a crown worn by the first king.
words.tr: 博物館最珍貴的寶物是第一位國王戴過的王冠。

tip_zh: in- 在這裡不是「沒有」，而是「價值大到無法估算」→ 極珍貴；valueless 真正「沒價值」；priceless 和 invaluable 同義「無價」
tip_en: invaluable = too valuable to measure, not "without value"; valueless = worthless; priceless = invaluable
trap: 看到 in-（不）+ valuable，學生以為是「沒價值」；其實與 priceless 同義。真正「沒價值」是 worthless / valueless。valueless／worthless 是「沒價值」，invaluable／priceless 卻是「無價之寶」，長得像、意思相反。

name: travesty/tragedy/parody

words.def_: an absurd or shocking distortion of something
words.sent: Holding the trial without allowing the defendant a lawyer was a travesty of justice.
words.tr: 不讓被告請律師就開審，根本是對正義的嘲弄。

words.sent: The collapse of the bridge was a tragedy that took dozens of lives.
words.tr: 大橋倒塌是一場奪走數十條人命的悲劇。
words.src: Hot Words L69；字根字首 U229

words.def_: a funny imitation that copies a style to make fun of it
words.sent: The comedy show performed a parody of the evening news, with puppets as reporters.
words.tr: 這個喜劇節目用玩偶當記者，演出晚間新聞的諧仿版。

tip_zh: travesty 不是旅行也不是悲劇，而是「拙劣的模仿、扭曲」（trans 變裝 + vest 衣服）；parody 諧仿（刻意模仿來搞笑）
tip_en: travesty = absurd distortion (dressed up badly); parody = humorous imitation
trap: 學生看到 trav- 想到 travel，或在 a travesty of justice 中把它當 tragedy；其實是「荒謬可笑的扭曲」。travesty 和 parody 都是「拙劣模仿」，但 parody 是故意搞笑，travesty 多指「荒謬的扭曲」。

name: penultimate/ultimate/ultimatum

words.sent: The mystery is solved in the penultimate chapter, and the final chapter shows the aftermath.
words.tr: 謎團在倒數第二章揭曉，最後一章則描寫後續。

words.sent: The ultimate goal of the project is to provide clean water to every village.
words.tr: 這項計畫的最終目標是為每個村莊提供乾淨的水。
words.src: Barron's U13；Hot Words L76；字根字首 U231

words.def_: a final demand with a threat if it is not met
words.sent: The landlord gave the tenants an ultimatum: pay the rent by Friday or leave.
words.tr: 房東對房客下最後通牒：週五前付租金，否則搬走。

tip_zh: pen- = paene「幾乎」→ penultimate 是「倒數第二」，不是「終極」；ultimatum 最後通牒（ultim 最後）
tip_en: penultimate = second to last; ultimatum = final demand
trap: 學生以為 penultimate 是「最最終的」，常在閱讀中誤解順序。ultimatum 是名詞，和 ultimate、penultimate 同字根 ultim（最後）。

name: indifferent/different

words.sent: Many voters seemed indifferent to the election, and turnout fell to a record low.
words.tr: 許多選民對選舉漠不關心，投票率創新低。
words.src: Hot Words L13；字根字首 U39

words.sent: The twins have very different personalities.
words.tr: 這對雙胞胎個性截然不同。

tip_zh: indifferent 不是「不不同 = 相同」，而是「漠不關心」
tip_en: indifferent = not caring
trap: 學生以為 in- + different = 沒差別 → 相同；其實是態度冷漠。

name: oversight/overlook/oversee

words.def_: supervision; an unintentional failure to notice
words.sent: Leaving the patient's allergy off the chart was a serious oversight.
words.tr: 沒把病人的過敏記在病歷上是一大疏失。

words.def_: to fail to notice; to ignore; to have a view from above
words.sent: The editor overlooked a typo in the headline, and readers noticed immediately.
words.tr: 編輯漏看了標題的錯字，讀者馬上就發現了。

words.sent: A new committee will oversee the construction of the bridge.
words.tr: 新委員會將監督大橋的興建。

tip_zh: oversight 有兩個相反意思：「監督」與「疏忽」；看上下文判斷；oversee 監督（over 在上 + see 看）
tip_en: oversight = supervision OR an unintentional mistake; oversee = supervise
trap: 學生只知道 over + sight =「看過去」，不知道它常指「疏失」或「監管」。oversee 是「監督」，overlook 卻常是「忽略」，oversight 兩個意思都有。

name: preposterous/prosperous/posterity

words.sent: The claim that the moon is made of cheese is preposterous.
words.tr: 說月亮是乳酪做的根本荒謬。

words.sent: The port grew into a prosperous city as trade with Asia expanded.
words.tr: 隨著與亞洲的貿易擴大，這個港口成為繁榮的城市。
words.src: Hot Words L58；字根字首 U213

words.sent: The diaries were saved for posterity in the national library.
words.tr: 這些日記被保存在國家圖書館，留給後世。

tip_zh: preposterous = pre（前）+ post（後）顛倒 → 荒謬至極；不是 prosperous（繁榮的）；posterity 後世（post 之後）
tip_en: preposterous = absurd (before and after reversed); posterity = future generations
trap: 字形與 prosperous 接近，學生常看錯成「繁榮的」。posterity 和 preposterous 都含 post（之後），preposterous 是「前後顛倒 → 荒謬」。

name: outlandish/exotic

words.sent: The singer was famous for her outlandish costumes, including a dress made of balloons.
words.tr: 這位歌手以古怪服裝聞名，包括一件氣球做的洋裝。

words.def_: from a distant country; strikingly unusual
words.sent: The garden displays exotic plants collected from rainforests around the world.
words.tr: 這座花園展示從世界各地雨林採集的奇異植物。

tip_zh: outlandish 字面是「外地來的」，現在指「古怪離譜的」；exotic 是「異國情調、新奇吸引人」
tip_en: outlandish = bizarre; exotic = interestingly foreign
trap: 學生以為 out + land = 外國的，誤以為與 exotic 同義；outlandish 帶貶義。

name: untoward/toward

words.sent: The flight landed safely, and passengers reported nothing untoward during the trip.
words.tr: 班機平安降落，乘客表示旅途中沒有任何異狀。

words.sent: The hikers walked toward the lake as the sun began to set.
words.tr: 太陽開始西下，健行者朝湖邊走去。

tip_zh: untoward 不是「不朝向」，而是「不適當的、意外不幸的」
tip_en: untoward = unexpected and inappropriate
trap: 學生以為 untoward 是 toward 的否定（方位），其實與方向無關。

name: unconscionable/unconscious

words.def_: not right or reasonable; shockingly unfair
words.sent: Charging sick patients ten times the normal price is unconscionable.
words.tr: 對病患收取正常價格十倍的費用實在喪盡天良。
words.src: Barron's U39；VA U34；字根字首 U16,73,150

words.sent: The diver was unconscious when the rescuers pulled him from the water.
words.tr: 救難人員把潛水員拉出水面時，他已失去意識。

tip_zh: unconscionable 來自 conscience（良心）→ 喪盡天良、過分的，不是「失去意識」
tip_en: unconscionable = morally unacceptable
trap: 字形像 unconscious，學生以為是「昏迷的」。

name: unassuming/assuming/presumptuous

words.sent: Despite her fame, the unassuming scientist still rode her bicycle to the lab every day.
words.tr: 儘管成名，這位謙遜的科學家仍每天騎腳踏車去實驗室。
words.src: Hot Words L71；字根字首 U73

words.def_: arrogant; taking too much for granted
words.sent: His assuming manner annoyed the committee, who felt he expected the job to be his.
words.tr: 他自以為是的態度惹惱了委員會，大家覺得他認定職位非他莫屬。

words.def_: too bold; acting without the right to do so
words.sent: It was presumptuous of him to start planning the victory party before the votes were counted.
words.tr: 選票還沒開完他就開始籌備慶功宴，實在太自以為是。
words.src: Hot Words L3；VA U26；字根字首 U60

tip_zh: unassuming 不是「不假設」，而是「謙遜、不擺架子」；assuming 作形容詞是「傲慢自大」；presumptuous 自以為是（presume 擅自認定），和 assuming 同義
tip_en: unassuming = modest; presumptuous = too bold
trap: 學生把 assume 理解為「假設」，於是誤讀 unassuming。presumptuous 和 assuming 都是「自以為是」，unassuming 才是「謙遜」。

name: infinitesimal/infinite

words.sent: The chance of being struck by a meteorite is infinitesimal.
words.tr: 被隕石擊中的機率微乎其微。

words.sent: She seemed to have infinite patience with her young students.
words.tr: 她對年幼的學生似乎有無限的耐心。

tip_zh: infinitesimal 不是「無限大」，而是「無限小、極微小」
tip_en: infinitesimal = extremely small
trap: 看到 infinite 就以為是「無窮大」，正好相反。

name: disinterested/uninterested

words.def_: not influenced by personal advantage; impartial
words.sent: The dispute was settled by a disinterested judge with no ties to either company.
words.tr: 這起糾紛由一位與兩家公司都無關係的公正法官裁決。
words.src: Hot Words L13；字根字首 U23

words.sent: The uninterested audience checked their phones throughout the lecture.
words.tr: 不感興趣的聽眾整場演講都在看手機。

tip_zh: disinterested = 沒有利害關係（interest 利益）→ 公正；uninterested 才是沒興趣
tip_en: disinterested = impartial; uninterested = bored
trap: dis- 像「不」，學生以為 disinterested 是「沒興趣」；SAT 用它表示「公正無私」。

name: noisome/noisy/noxious

words.def_: having an extremely bad smell; harmful
words.sent: A noisome odor rose from the swamp in the summer heat.
words.tr: 夏日炎熱中，沼澤散發令人作嘔的惡臭。
words.src: Barron's U34；VA U22；字根字首 U204

words.sent: The noisy construction outside made it impossible to concentrate.
words.tr: 外面吵鬧的施工讓人根本無法專心。

words.sent: The factory was fined for releasing noxious gases into the air.
words.tr: 這家工廠因排放有毒氣體到空氣中而被罰款。
words.src: Hot Words L11；306/386 U19；字根字首 U204

tip_zh: noisome 和 noise 無關，來自 annoy → 令人作嘔、有害；noxious 有毒的（nox 傷害），意思接近 noisome
tip_en: noisome comes from "annoy": offensive, foul-smelling; noxious = harmful, poisonous
trap: 看到 noise 就以為是「吵鬧的」；noisome 是指氣味噁心或有害。noisome、noxious 都是「有害、難聞」，跟 noise（噪音）毫無關係。

name: bemused/amused/muse

words.sent: He gave a bemused look at the instructions, which were printed only in Finnish.
words.tr: 他困惑地看著只印芬蘭文的說明書。

words.sent: The children were amused by the clown's oversized shoes.
words.tr: 孩子們被小丑的超大鞋子逗樂了。

words.sent: Sitting by the window, she began to muse about what her life would be like in ten years.
words.tr: 她坐在窗邊，開始沉思十年後的生活會是什麼樣子。

tip_zh: bemused = 困惑出神（be- 使…處在 muse 沉思中）；amused 才是覺得好笑；muse 沉思（bemused 的字源：被困在沉思中）
tip_en: bemused = puzzled; amused = entertained; muse = think deeply
trap: 看起來像 amused 加了 be-，學生常以為是「被逗樂」。bemused 來自 muse（沉思），所以是「困惑出神」，不是 amused（被逗樂）。

name: fulsome/full/wholesome

words.zh: 過分恭維的；虛情假意的
words.sent: The employees' fulsome praise of the new boss sounded more like fear than admiration.
words.tr: 員工對新上司過分的讚美聽來更像害怕而非欽佩。
words.src: Barron's U21；Hot Words L50；字根字首 U186

words.def_: containing as much as possible; complete
words.sent: The report gives a full account of what happened on the night of the fire.
words.tr: 這份報告完整交代火災當晚發生的事。

words.def_: good for health or moral well-being
words.sent: The school replaced soda machines with wholesome snacks like fruit and nuts.
words.tr: 學校把汽水販賣機換成水果、堅果等健康零食。

tip_zh: fulsome 不是「充分的」，而是「過分、虛偽地」稱讚（讚美多到令人反感）；wholesome 有益健康的（-some 表「具有…性質」）
tip_en: fulsome = excessive and insincere, not just "full"; wholesome = healthy
trap: 看到 full 就以為是「豐富、充分的」；SAT 中 fulsome praise 帶貶義。fulsome 和 wholesome 都是 -some 結尾，fulsome 卻是負面的「過分恭維」。

name: inchoate/chaotic

words.def_: just begun and not fully formed
words.sent: Her plan for the novel was still inchoate: a few characters and a vague idea for the ending.
words.tr: 她的小說構想仍未成形：只有幾個角色和模糊的結局想法。
words.src: Barron's U13；VA U17；字根字首 U42

words.sent: The first day of the sale was chaotic, with shoppers pushing past one another.
words.tr: 特賣第一天一片混亂，購物者互相推擠。

tip_zh: inchoate 與 chaos 無關，意思是「剛起步、尚未成形」（incohare 開始）
tip_en: inchoate = just begun, undeveloped
trap: 中間的 -choate 看起來像 chaos，學生以為是「混亂的」。

name: apposite/opposite

words.sent: The speaker opened with an apposite quotation that perfectly captured the theme of the conference.
words.tr: 講者以一句切題的引言開場，完美點出研討會主題。

words.sent: The two scientists reached opposite conclusions from the same data.
words.tr: 兩位科學家從相同資料得出相反結論。

tip_zh: apposite 是「恰當的、切題的」（ap- 靠近 + posit 放 → 放得剛好），不是 opposite
tip_en: apposite = apt, relevant
trap: 只差第一個字母，學生直覺讀成 opposite（相反的）。

name: uncanny/canny/uncouth

words.def_: strange in a way that is hard to explain
words.sent: The actor bore an uncanny resemblance to the president he portrayed.
words.tr: 這位演員與他飾演的總統長得像得不可思議。

words.def_: shrewd, especially with money or business
words.sent: A canny investor, he bought land near the station years before the train line opened.
words.tr: 他是精明的投資人，在鐵路通車前數年就買下車站附近土地。
words.src: Hot Words L28；字根字首 U170

words.sent: His uncouth habit of talking with his mouth full embarrassed his date.
words.tr: 他滿嘴食物還講話的粗魯習慣，讓約會對象很尷尬。
words.src: Hot Words L87；字根字首 U231

tip_zh: uncanny 不是「不精明」，而是「詭異得不可思議」；canny = 精明；uncouth 粗魯的（couth 古字「熟悉的」，現在幾乎不單獨用）
tip_en: uncanny = strangely unnatural, not "not shrewd"; uncouth = rude
trap: un- 讓人以為與 canny 相反，其實兩者意思無關。uncouth 和 uncanny 一樣是 un- 開頭，但原字 couth 幾乎不用，別以為有對應的「正面字」。

name: unravel/ravel

words.def_: to untangle; to solve; to fall apart
words.sent: Detectives worked for months to unravel the mystery of the missing painting.
words.tr: 偵探花了數月才揭開名畫失蹤之謎。

words.sent: The old sweater began to ravel at the cuffs after years of wear.
words.tr: 這件舊毛衣穿了多年，袖口開始散線。

tip_zh: un- 沒有反轉意思：ravel 和 unravel 都可指「解開、拆散」；比喻用法 unravel = 瓦解、解開謎團
tip_en: ravel and unravel can both mean "untangle"
trap: 學生以為 un- 一定是相反，把 ravel 當「打結」；其實兩字常同義。

name: indefatigable/invincible

words.zh: 不知疲倦的；不屈不撓的
words.sent: The indefatigable volunteer worked twelve-hour days to rebuild homes after the flood.
words.tr: 這位不知疲倦的志工每天工作十二小時重建災後家園。
words.src: Hot Words L56；VA U29；字根字首 U39

words.sent: After ten straight wins, the team began to believe it was invincible.
words.tr: 連勝十場後，這支隊伍開始相信自己天下無敵。

tip_zh: indefatigable 裡是 fatigue（疲倦），不是 defeat → 不知疲倦的
tip_en: indefatigable = tireless (fatigue), not "undefeatable"
trap: 學生看到 defat- 以為是 defeat → 「無法被打敗的」；不可戰勝是 invincible。

name: histrionic/historic/historical

words.sent: His histrionic complaints about a cold coffee made the other customers roll their eyes.
words.tr: 他為一杯冷掉的咖啡誇張抱怨，讓其他顧客翻白眼。

words.sent: The moon landing was a historic achievement watched by millions.
words.tr: 登月是數百萬人觀看的歷史性成就。

words.def_: relating to history or the past
words.sent: The museum displays historical documents from the colonial period.
words.tr: 博物館展示殖民時期的歷史文件。

tip_zh: histrionic 和 history 無關，來自 histrio（演員）→ 誇張做作、像演戲；historical 有關歷史的（historic 是「具歷史意義的」）
tip_en: histrionic = overly dramatic; historical = relating to history
trap: 學生看到 histor- 以為是「歷史的」。historic 和 historical 常被混用：historic 是「歷史性的、重大的」，historical 只是「與歷史有關」；histrionic 則和歷史無關。

name: decimate/decimal

words.def_: to kill or destroy a large part of
words.sent: A fungal disease decimated the frog population, wiping out entire species.
words.tr: 一種真菌疾病使蛙類大量死亡，數個物種因此滅絕。

words.def_: based on the number ten; a number with a decimal point
words.sent: Most countries use a decimal currency, with one hundred cents in a dollar.
words.tr: 多數國家使用十進位貨幣，一元等於一百分。

tip_zh: decimate 原指「十人殺一」，現在指「大量毀滅」，和小數點無關
tip_en: decimate = destroy a large part of
trap: 看到 deci- 以為與「十、小數」有關，或以為只毀掉十分之一。

name: effete/effective/efficacious

words.sent: The aging empire was ruled by an effete aristocracy more interested in parties than defense.
words.tr: 衰老的帝國由頹廢的貴族統治，他們熱衷派對勝過國防。

words.sent: The new vaccine was highly effective, preventing nine out of ten infections.
words.tr: 新疫苗非常有效，可預防九成的感染。

words.sent: Rest and fluids remain the most efficacious treatment for the common cold.
words.tr: 休息和多喝水仍是治感冒最有效的方法。

tip_zh: effete 不是 effective，而是「衰弱無力、頹廢軟弱」（原指生育後耗盡）；efficacious 有效的（＝ effective，SAT 常用的正式字）
tip_en: effete = weak, decadent; efficacious = effective
trap: 看到 eff- 以為與 effect、effective 相關，誤解為「有效的」。efficacious 和 effective 同義，effete 卻是「衰弱頹廢」。

name: disabuse/abuse

words.def_: to persuade someone that a belief is wrong
words.sent: The tour guide quickly disabused visitors of the idea that the castle was haunted.
words.tr: 導遊很快就打破遊客以為城堡鬧鬼的想法。

words.sent: Officials were accused of abusing their power to reward friends with contracts.
words.tr: 官員被控濫用職權，把合約給朋友作為回報。
words.src: Hot Words L51；字根字首 U1

tip_zh: disabuse 不是「不虐待」，而是「解除錯誤觀念、使醒悟」
tip_en: disabuse = free someone from a false belief
trap: 學生以為 dis- + abuse = 停止虐待；其實和虐待無關。

name: unwonted/unwanted/wont

words.sent: The normally quiet librarian spoke with unwonted anger about the budget cuts.
words.tr: 平常安靜的圖書館員一反常態，憤怒地談論預算刪減。

words.sent: The app blocks unwanted calls from telemarketers.
words.tr: 這個應用程式能封鎖電話行銷的騷擾來電。

words.sent: As was his wont, the professor arrived exactly five minutes early.
words.tr: 照他的習慣，教授剛好提早五分鐘到。

tip_zh: unwonted 來自 wont（習慣）→ 不尋常的；不是 unwanted（不想要的）；wont 習慣（as is his wont），unwonted ＝ 不合習慣
tip_en: unwonted = unusual; wont = habit
trap: 只差一個字母，學生直接讀成 unwanted。wont 不是 won't；unwonted 正是由 wont（習慣）加 un- 而來。

name: inured/injured/insured

words.sent: Years in the arctic had inured the scientist to temperatures that would shock most visitors.
words.tr: 在北極多年，這位科學家已習慣讓多數訪客震驚的低溫。

words.sent: The injured player was carried off the field on a stretcher.
words.tr: 受傷的球員被擔架抬出場。

words.sent: Because the car was insured, the repairs cost the owner nothing.
words.tr: 因為車子有保險，車主不用付任何修理費。

tip_zh: inured 是「習以為常、變得麻木」（in + ure 使用到習慣），不是 injured；insured 有保險的（insure）
tip_en: inured = accustomed to hardship; insured = covered by insurance
trap: 字形像 injured，學生以為是「受傷的」。inured、injured、insured 只差一個字母：習慣、受傷、有保險。

name: impertinent/pertinent/pertinacious

words.sent: The reporter's impertinent question about the actor's divorce ended the interview.
words.tr: 記者問演員離婚的無禮問題讓訪問就此結束。

words.sent: Please include only pertinent details in your summary.
words.tr: 摘要中請只寫相關的細節。

words.def_: holding firmly to an opinion or purpose; stubborn
words.sent: The pertinacious reporter kept asking the same question until the minister finally answered.
words.tr: 那位執著的記者一再追問同一個問題，直到部長終於回答。

tip_zh: impertinent 除了「不相關」，更常用為「無禮、冒失」；pertinacious 頑固執著（per- 徹底 + tenac 緊抓）
tip_en: impertinent = rude, not only "not pertinent"; pertinacious = stubbornly persistent
trap: 學生只想到「不切題」，SAT 卻常用它形容無禮的態度。pertinacious 長得像 pertinent，其實和 tenacious 同源，意思是「死纏不放」。

name: disaffected/unaffected/affected

words.sent: Disaffected voters, tired of broken promises, turned to a new party.
words.tr: 厭倦了跳票的不滿選民轉而支持新政黨。
words.src: Hot Words L63；字根字首 U22

words.zh: 不受影響的；自然真誠的
words.sent: Rural areas were largely unaffected by the power outage.
words.tr: 鄉村地區大致未受停電影響。

words.sent: His affected British accent disappeared as soon as he got angry.
words.tr: 他一生氣，那做作的英國腔就不見了。

tip_zh: disaffected 不是「不受影響」，而是「不滿、疏離（失去 affection 好感）」；affected 作形容詞常是「做作的」，不只是「受影響的」
tip_en: disaffected = dissatisfied, alienated; affected = artificial, pretentious
trap: 學生以為 dis- + affected = 沒受影響；真正「不受影響」是 unaffected。affected 除了「受影響」，SAT 常考「做作」；unaffected 也可指「真誠自然」。

name: untold/unsaid

words.def_: too great to be counted or measured
words.sent: The hurricane caused untold damage along the coast.
words.tr: 颶風在沿岸造成難以估量的損害。

words.sent: Some things are better left unsaid at a family dinner.
words.tr: 有些話在家庭聚餐時還是別說出口比較好。

tip_zh: untold 常指「數不清的、極大的」（untold damage），不只是「沒說出來」
tip_en: untold = too great to count
trap: 學生以為 untold = 沒被說出的；閱讀中 untold millions 指「無數」。

name: cavalier/chivalrous

words.def_: showing a careless lack of concern
words.sent: His cavalier attitude toward safety rules put the whole crew at risk.
words.tr: 他對安全規定滿不在乎的態度讓全體人員陷入危險。

words.def_: courteous and honorable, especially toward others in need
words.zh: 有騎士風度的；彬彬有禮的
words.sent: In a chivalrous gesture, he gave his seat to the elderly woman.
words.tr: 他很有風度地把座位讓給那位老太太。
words.src: Hot Words L38；字根字首 U172

tip_zh: cavalier 原指騎士，但形容詞是「傲慢、漫不經心的」；有騎士風度是 chivalrous
tip_en: cavalier = dismissive, offhand
trap: 學生看到「騎士」就以為是讚美，其實是負面的「輕率傲慢」。

name: superfluous/superlative/superficial/supercilious

words.sent: The editor cut every superfluous word, shortening the article by half.
words.tr: 編輯刪掉所有多餘的字，文章縮短了一半。
words.src: Barron's U37；Hot Words L83；字根字首 U66

words.sent: The museum is famous for its superlative collection of ancient coins.
words.tr: 這座博物館以頂尖的古錢幣收藏聞名。

words.def_: concerned only with the surface; not deep
words.sent: The report gave only a superficial analysis and ignored the real causes of the problem.
words.tr: 這份報告只做了膚淺的分析，忽略問題的真正原因。
words.src: Barron's U26；Hot Words L27；306/386 U27；字根字首 U66,104

words.def_: behaving as if one is better than others
words.sent: The supercilious waiter looked down at customers who could not pronounce the French dishes.
words.tr: 那個傲慢的服務生瞧不起不會唸法國菜名的客人。
words.src: Hot Words L3；VA U13；字根字首 U66

tip_zh: superfluous 的 super- 是「超過」→ 多餘的，不是「超讚」；最好的是 superlative；superficial 膚淺的（super 上 + face 表面）；supercilious 傲慢（cilium 眉毛 → 挑眉看人）
tip_en: superfluous = more than needed; superficial = shallow; supercilious = arrogant
trap: 學生以為 super- 一定是「超級好」。四字都以 super- 開頭，但只有 superlative 是「最好的」。

name: restive/restful/restless

words.def_: unable to stay still; impatient under control
words.zh: 焦躁不安的；難以駕馭的
words.sent: The crowd grew restive as the concert was delayed for a second hour.
words.tr: 演唱會延誤第二個小時，群眾愈來愈焦躁。
words.src: Hot Words L61；字根字首 U62,134

words.sent: The garden offered a restful place to read after work.
words.tr: 這座花園是下班後讀書的寧靜去處。

words.def_: unable to stay still or relax
words.sent: The restless child kept kicking the seat in front of him during the long flight.
words.tr: 長途飛行中，那個坐不住的孩子一直踢前面的座椅。

tip_zh: restive 不是「休息」，而是「不安、難駕馭」（像不肯前進的馬）；restless 坐立不安，和 restive 意思接近
tip_en: restive = restless, impatient; restful = calm; restless = unable to keep still
trap: 看到 rest 就以為是「平靜的」；restive 恰好相反。restive 和 restless 都是「不安」，restful 才是「讓人放鬆」。

name: redoubtable/doubtful

words.sent: The young player faced a redoubtable opponent who had not lost a match in two years.
words.tr: 這位年輕選手面對兩年未嘗敗績的可畏對手。

words.sent: It is doubtful that the museum will reopen before next spring.
words.tr: 博物館能否在明年春天前重新開放，令人存疑。
words.src: Hot Words L66；字根字首 U179

tip_zh: redoubtable 來自 doubt 的古義「害怕」→ 令人敬畏的，不是「可疑的」
tip_en: redoubtable = formidable, worthy of respect
trap: 看到 doubt 就以為是「值得懷疑的」，其實是「令人生畏、可敬的對手」。

name: meretricious/meritorious

words.def_: attractive on the surface but of little value
words.sent: The film's meretricious special effects could not hide its weak story.
words.tr: 電影華而不實的特效掩蓋不了薄弱的劇情。

words.sent: The soldier received a medal for meritorious service during the rescue.
words.tr: 這名士兵因救援期間的卓越表現而獲頒勳章。

tip_zh: meretricious 和 merit 無關，意思是「華而不實、俗豔的」（拉丁文 meretrix）
tip_en: meretricious = showy but worthless
trap: 看到 mer- 以為與 merit（優點）相關，誤解為「值得稱讚的」；值得稱讚是 meritorious。

name: impregnable/impregnate/impenetrable

words.def_: unable to be captured or broken into
words.sent: The castle sat on a cliff, making it nearly impregnable to attackers.
words.tr: 城堡建在懸崖上，敵人幾乎攻不破。

words.def_: to soak or fill with a substance; to make pregnant
words.sent: The wood is impregnated with oil to protect it from rain.
words.tr: 木材以油浸透，以防雨水侵蝕。

words.def_: impossible to enter or go through; impossible to understand
words.sent: The jungle was so thick that it was nearly impenetrable.
words.tr: 叢林茂密到幾乎無法穿越。
words.src: Hot Words L49；306/386 U14；字根字首 U38

tip_zh: impregnable = im-（不）+ prehendere（抓住）→ 攻不破的；與懷孕的 impregnate 無關；impenetrable 無法穿越的（penetrate 穿透），和 impregnable 意思接近
tip_en: impregnable = unable to be captured; impenetrable = impossible to pass through
trap: 學生看到 pregn- 聯想到 pregnant，搞錯意思。impregnable 和 impenetrable 都表示「進不去」，但 impregnable 多用於城堡、立場「攻不破」。

name: nondescript/indescribable

words.sent: The spy chose a nondescript gray car so that no one would notice him.
words.tr: 間諜挑了一輛毫不起眼的灰色車，以免被人注意。

words.def_: too extreme or unusual to be described
words.sent: The view from the summit was indescribable, stretching across three countries.
words.tr: 山頂的景色難以形容，可遠眺三個國家。

tip_zh: nondescript 不是「無法形容的」，而是「普通到沒什麼好形容」→ 平淡無奇
tip_en: nondescript = dull, lacking distinctive features
trap: 學生以為 non- + describe = 難以形容（很厲害）；其實是「毫無特色」。

name: antediluvian/antidote/antecedent/antipathy

words.sent: The office still used an antediluvian computer system that could not open email attachments.
words.tr: 辦公室還在用連郵件附件都開不了的老古董電腦系統。
words.src: Hot Words L24；字根字首 U162

words.def_: a medicine that counteracts poison; a remedy
words.sent: Laughter can be an antidote to stress.
words.tr: 笑聲可以是壓力的解藥。
words.src: Hot Words L31；字根字首 U5

words.sent: The abacus is an early antecedent of the modern calculator.
words.tr: 算盤是現代計算機的早期前身。

words.sent: Her antipathy toward cruelty to animals led her to become a vegetarian.
words.tr: 她對虐待動物的厭惡讓她成為素食者。
words.src: Barron's U37；306/386 U3；字根字首 U5,115

tip_zh: ante- 是「之前」（不是 anti- 反對）：antediluvian = 大洪水之前 → 極古老過時；antecedent 前身（ante- 之前）；antipathy 反感（anti- 反對 + path 感覺）
tip_en: ante- = before; anti- = against; antecedent = forerunner; antipathy = strong dislike
trap: 學生把 ante- 和 anti- 混為一談，以為 antediluvian 是「反洪水的」。ante-（之前）：antediluvian、antecedent；anti-（反對）：antidote、antipathy，只差一個字母。

name: sanctimonious/saintly/sanctity

words.zh: 道貌岸然的；假裝聖潔的
words.sent: The sanctimonious politician lectured others about honesty while hiding his own debts.
words.tr: 這位道貌岸然的政客教訓別人要誠實，卻隱瞞自己的債務。
words.src: Barron's U35；VA U18；字根字首 U128,219

words.def_: very good and kind, like a saint
words.sent: Her saintly patience with difficult patients made her the most beloved nurse in the ward.
words.tr: 她對難搞病人聖人般的耐心，讓她成為病房最受愛戴的護理師。

words.def_: holiness; the quality of being very important
words.sent: The court stressed the sanctity of human life in its ruling.
words.tr: 法院在判決中強調人命的神聖。

tip_zh: sanctimonious 不是「神聖的」，而是「假裝虔誠、道貌岸然」；sanctity 神聖（n.，正面）
tip_en: sanctimonious = hypocritically pious; sanctity = holiness
trap: 看到 sanct-（神聖）以為是讚美，其實是貶義。sanctity 是真的神聖，sanctimonious 卻是「假裝神聖」。

name: prepossessing/possessive/unprepossessing

words.zh: 討人喜歡的；有吸引力的
words.sent: The restaurant's entrance was not prepossessing, but the food inside was excellent.
words.tr: 餐廳門口並不起眼，裡面的食物卻非常出色。

words.def_: demanding someone's total attention; unwilling to share
words.sent: The possessive child refused to let anyone else touch his toys.
words.tr: 佔有慾強的孩子不准任何人碰他的玩具。

words.sent: Despite its unprepossessing appearance, the little shop sells the best dumplings in the city.
words.tr: 儘管外表不起眼，這家小店賣的是全市最好吃的餃子。

tip_zh: prepossessing 是「討人喜歡、有吸引力的」（預先佔據你的好感），與 possessive（佔有慾強）無關；unprepossessing 不起眼（prepossessing 的反義）
tip_en: prepossessing = attractive, appealing; unprepossessing = unattractive
trap: 看到 possess 以為與「佔有」有關；unprepossessing 則是「不起眼的」。unprepossessing 是 prepossessing 的反義，兩者都和「佔有」無關。

name: enervate/energize/venerate

words.def_: to weaken; to drain of energy
words.sent: The humid heat enervated the runners, and many slowed to a walk.
words.tr: 潮濕的酷熱讓跑者筋疲力盡，許多人放慢成步行。
words.src: Hot Words L47；VA U15；字根字首 U27

words.def_: to give energy and enthusiasm to
words.sent: The coach's speech energized the team before the final match.
words.tr: 教練的演說在決賽前激勵了全隊。

words.sent: Many cultures venerate their ancestors with yearly ceremonies.
words.tr: 許多文化每年舉行儀式來敬拜祖先。
words.src: Hot Words L19,79；VA U8；字根字首 U128,232

tip_zh: e- 是「抽出」，nerv 神經 → 把神經力氣抽掉 → 使衰弱，與 energize 相反；venerate 尊敬（vener 尊崇）
tip_en: enervate = drain energy (e- out + nerve); venerate = respect deeply
trap: enervate 看起來像 energy + ate，學生常以為是「使充滿活力」，其實正好相反。venerate 和 enervate 字母幾乎一樣，只是排列不同，意思完全無關。

name: nonplussed/unfazed

words.def_: so surprised and confused that one does not know how to react
words.sent: The candidate was nonplussed by the unexpected question and paused for a long time.
words.tr: 候選人被意料外的問題問倒，愣了好久。

words.sent: Unfazed by the heckling, the speaker continued with her presentation.
words.tr: 演講者對喝倒彩毫不在意，繼續報告。

tip_zh: nonplussed = 困惑不知所措（non plus 「無法更多」→ 卡住了）；不受影響是 unfazed
tip_en: nonplussed = baffled, not calm
trap: non- 讓人以為是「不困擾」，連母語人士都常誤用成「淡定」；SAT 以原義「困惑」為準。

name: temerity/timidity

words.sent: The intern had the temerity to correct the CEO in front of the entire board.
words.tr: 這位實習生竟敢在全體董事面前糾正執行長。
words.src: Barron's U16；306/386 U28；VA U21；字根字首 U228

words.sent: Her timidity kept her from asking questions, even when she was confused.
words.tr: 她的膽怯讓她即使困惑也不敢發問。

tip_zh: temerity 與 timid 相反：「魯莽、膽大包天」（temere 盲目地）
tip_en: temerity = reckless boldness
trap: temerity 長得像 timidity，學生常以為是「膽怯」。

name: impassive/impassioned/passive

words.sent: The judge remained impassive as the verdict was read, revealing nothing of her feelings.
words.tr: 宣讀判決時法官面無表情，絲毫不透露情緒。
words.src: Hot Words L13；字根字首 U36

words.sent: The student gave an impassioned speech urging the school to ban plastic bottles.
words.tr: 這名學生發表激昂演說，呼籲學校禁用塑膠瓶。

words.def_: accepting what happens without active response
words.sent: Instead of waiting in a passive way for help, the villagers began rebuilding the bridge themselves.
words.tr: 村民沒有被動地等待援助，而是自己動手重建橋樑。

tip_zh: im- + passive 不是「不被動 → 主動激動」；impassive 來自 passion → 「沒有情緒的」；passive 被動的（impassive 的陷阱來源）
tip_en: impassive = expressionless (without passion); passive = not acting
trap: 學生以為 impassive = not passive = 熱烈，其實是「面無表情」；熱烈激昂是 impassioned。impassive 看起來像 im- ＋ passive，其實和 passive 意思完全無關。

name: enormity/enormousness

words.def_: great wickedness; the extreme seriousness of something bad
words.zh: 滔天大罪；（壞事的）嚴重性
words.sent: Only after visiting the camp did she grasp the enormity of the crimes committed there.
words.tr: 親自走訪集中營後，她才理解那裡犯下的罪行有多麼深重。

words.sent: Visitors are struck by the sheer enormousness of the canyon.
words.tr: 遊客都為峽谷的龐大而震撼。

tip_zh: enormity 的正式意思是「滔天大罪、極度邪惡」，不只是「巨大」；單純「龐大」用 enormousness
tip_en: enormity = great wickedness
trap: 看到 enorm- 以為等於「巨大」，SAT 正式文章中 enormity 多指罪行之嚴重。

name: inhabitable/uninhabitable/habitable

words.sent: Engineers are studying whether underground caves on Mars could be made inhabitable.
words.tr: 工程師正研究火星地下洞穴能否改造成適合居住。

words.sent: The earthquake left half the buildings in the town uninhabitable.
words.tr: 地震使鎮上半數建築無法居住。

words.sent: Scientists search for planets with liquid water that might be habitable.
words.tr: 科學家尋找可能有液態水、適合居住的行星。

tip_zh: inhabitable 的 in- 是「在裡面」→ 可居住的（= habitable）；不能住是 uninhabitable；habitable 可居住的，和 inhabitable 同義
tip_en: inhabitable = habitable; habitable = livable
trap: 跟 inflammable 一樣，學生以為 in- 是否定，把「可居住」誤解為「不可居住」。habitable、inhabitable 意思一樣，只有 uninhabitable 才是「不能住」。

name: spendthrift/thrifty

words.def_: a person who spends money wastefully
words.sent: The spendthrift prince sold the family jewels to pay his gambling debts.
words.tr: 揮霍的王子變賣家傳珠寶來償還賭債。
words.src: Hot Words L8；VA U4；字根字首 U224

words.sent: Thrifty shoppers wait for sales before buying winter coats.
words.tr: 節儉的購物者會等特價再買冬季大衣。
words.src: Hot Words L9；字根字首 U229

tip_zh: spendthrift 不是「節儉」，而是「揮霍的人」（把 thrift 積蓄 spend 光）
tip_en: spendthrift = wasteful spender
trap: 看到 thrift（節儉）以為是正面，其實意思相反。

name: inflammable/nonflammable/flammable/inflammatory

words.def_: easily set on fire (same as flammable)
words.sent: Keep inflammable liquids such as gasoline away from heaters and open flames.
words.tr: 汽油等易燃液體應遠離暖氣與明火。

words.sent: Theater curtains must be made of nonflammable fabric.
words.tr: 劇院布幕必須使用不易燃的布料。

words.sent: Paint thinner is highly flammable, so never use it near a stove.
words.tr: 油漆稀釋劑非常易燃，絕不可在爐子旁使用。

words.def_: likely to cause anger or violence; causing swelling
words.sent: The politician's inflammatory speech led to fights in the streets.
words.tr: 那位政客的煽動性演說引發街頭衝突。

tip_zh: inflammable 的 in- 是「進入（火焰）」，= flammable 易燃；不易燃要用 nonflammable；flammable 易燃（＝ inflammable）；inflammatory 煽動性的、發炎的
tip_en: in- here means "into flame," so inflammable = flammable; flammable = inflammable; inflammatory = provocative
trap: 學生以為 in- 是否定，把 inflammable 當「不可燃」，在安全標示上會出大錯。inflammable 和 flammable 同義；inflammatory 則多指言論「煽動」或身體「發炎」。

name: ingratiate/ingratitude/ingrate

words.def_: to gain favor by flattery or effort
words.sent: The new employee tried to ingratiate himself with the boss by bringing her coffee every morning.
words.tr: 新員工每天早上幫上司買咖啡，試圖討好她。
words.src: Barron's U36；Hot Words L50；字根字首 U43,155

words.sent: After all her help, his ingratitude hurt her deeply.
words.tr: 她幫了那麼多，他的忘恩負義讓她很受傷。

words.sent: After all the help his friends gave him, only an ingrate would refuse to visit them in the hospital.
words.tr: 朋友幫了他那麼多，只有忘恩負義的人才會連去醫院探望都不肯。

tip_zh: ingratiate 不是「忘恩」，而是「討好、巴結」（in + gratia 好感 → 進入別人好感）；ingrate 忘恩負義的人（n.，ingratitude 是這種行為）
tip_en: ingratiate = win favor; ingrate = ungrateful person
trap: 看到 ingrat- 以為與 ingratitude（忘恩負義）相關。ingrate 才真正和 ingratitude 相關；ingratiate 是「討好」。

name: unexceptionable/unexceptional

words.def_: not open to objection; beyond criticism
words.sent: Her conduct throughout the investigation was unexceptionable.
words.tr: 她在整個調查期間的表現無可挑剔。

words.sent: The hotel was clean but unexceptional, much like every other hotel on the highway.
words.tr: 這家旅館乾淨但很普通，就像公路旁其他旅館一樣。

tip_zh: unexceptionable = 無可挑剔（找不到 exception 可以反對）；unexceptional = 平凡普通
tip_en: unexceptionable = beyond criticism; unexceptional = ordinary
trap: 兩字只差 -able，學生以為意思一樣，其實一個是讚美，一個是平淡。

name: novel

words.sent: The novel follows three generations of a family living in the same small town.
words.tr: 這部小說講述同一座小鎮中一家三代的故事。
words.src: Hot Words L24,85；306/386 U19；字根字首 U114

words.sent: Researchers took a novel approach, using drones to count the whales instead of boats.
words.tr: 研究人員採用新穎的方法，用無人機而非船隻來計算鯨魚數量。
words.src: Hot Words L24,85；306/386 U19；字根字首 U114

tip_zh: n. 小說 → adj. 新穎的（novice 新手、innovate 創新同源）
tip_en: noun: a book; adjective: new and original
trap: 學生只認得「小說」，看到 a novel approach 就卡住。

name: flag

words.def_: a piece of cloth used as a symbol
words.sent: The flag was lowered to half-mast to honor the victims.
words.tr: 為悼念罹難者，國旗降半旗。
words.src: Hot Words L45；字根字首 U184

words.sent: By the fourth hour of the meeting, attention began to flag, and several people checked their phones.
words.tr: 會議進行到第四小時，大家注意力開始渙散，有幾人看起手機。
words.src: Hot Words L45；字根字首 U184

tip_zh: n. 旗子 → v. 減弱、衰退（旗子無風垂下）；也作「標記」
tip_en: noun: a banner; verb: to weaken, to lose energy
trap: SAT 常考 flagging interest／his energy flagged，學生會誤解成「插旗」。

name: champion

words.sent: The defending champion lost in the first round of the tournament.
words.tr: 衛冕冠軍在錦標賽第一輪就落敗。

words.def_: to support or defend a cause
words.sent: She championed the rights of farm workers for more than forty years.
words.tr: 她四十多年來一直為農場工人的權益奮鬥。

tip_zh: n. 冠軍 → v. 擁護、為…奮鬥
tip_en: noun: winner; verb: to fight for a cause
trap: champion 當動詞時與比賽無關，是「倡導、捍衛」。

name: compromise

words.def_: an agreement in which each side gives up something
words.sent: After hours of debate, the two parties reached a compromise on the budget.
words.tr: 經過數小時辯論，兩黨就預算達成妥協。

words.sent: Sharing your password can compromise the security of the entire network.
words.tr: 分享密碼可能危及整個網路的安全。

tip_zh: n./v. 妥協 → v. 損害、危及（compromise security）
tip_en: to settle by concession; to endanger or weaken
trap: 學生只知道「妥協」，看到 compromise the system 會誤解成「與系統妥協」。

name: conviction

words.def_: a formal declaration that someone is guilty
words.sent: The new evidence led to the overturning of his conviction.
words.tr: 新證據使他的有罪判決被推翻。
words.src: Hot Words L67；字根字首 U97

words.sent: She spoke with conviction, sure that the plan would work.
words.tr: 她堅定地說著，確信計畫會成功。
words.src: Hot Words L67；字根字首 U97

tip_zh: 定罪（convict 罪犯）→ 堅定的信念（convinced 深信）
tip_en: a guilty verdict; a firmly held belief
trap: SAT 常用 conviction 指「信念」，學生容易聯想到犯罪。

name: entertain

words.sent: The magician entertained the children with tricks for an hour.
words.tr: 魔術師用戲法逗孩子們玩了一小時。

words.def_: to consider an idea or feeling
words.sent: The committee refused to entertain any proposal that would raise taxes.
words.tr: 委員會拒絕考慮任何會加稅的提案。

tip_zh: 娛樂 → 考慮、心存（entertain an idea/doubt）
tip_en: to amuse; to consider an idea
trap: entertain the possibility 是「考慮這種可能性」，不是娛樂。

name: exploit

words.def_: to use unfairly for one's own advantage
words.sent: The factory exploited child workers, paying them almost nothing.
words.tr: 這家工廠剝削童工，幾乎不付薪水。
words.src: Barron's U28；306/386 U11；字根字首 U28

words.sent: The book recounts the explorer's exploits in the Antarctic.
words.tr: 這本書記述探險家在南極的英勇事蹟。
words.src: Barron's U28；306/386 U11；字根字首 U28

tip_zh: v. 利用、剝削 → n. 英勇事蹟、功績（重音在前 EX-ploit）
tip_en: verb: to use unfairly; noun: a bold heroic deed
trap: SAT 閱讀中 exploits 常指「冒險事蹟」，學生只知道負面的「剝削」。

name: gravity

words.def_: the force that pulls objects toward the earth
words.sent: Because the moon's gravity is weaker, astronauts can jump much higher there.
words.tr: 月球重力較弱，太空人在那裡能跳得高得多。

words.sent: The doctor's tone made clear the gravity of the diagnosis.
words.tr: 醫師的語氣清楚表明診斷結果的嚴重性。

tip_zh: 重力 → 嚴重性、莊重（grave 嚴重的）
tip_en: the force pulling objects; seriousness
trap: the gravity of the situation 是「情況的嚴重性」，不是物理。

name: harbor

words.def_: a sheltered area of water for ships
words.sent: Fishing boats returned to the harbor before the storm.
words.tr: 漁船在暴風雨前返回港口。

words.def_: to keep a thought or feeling in one's mind
words.sent: Although he smiled, he still harbored doubts about the plan.
words.tr: 雖然他笑著，心裡仍對計畫存有疑慮。

tip_zh: n. 港口 → v. 心懷（harbor doubts／a grudge）、窩藏
tip_en: noun: port; verb: to hold a feeling, to shelter
trap: harbor resentment 是「懷恨在心」，學生常卡在「港口」。

name: minute

words.sent: The train leaves in five minutes.
words.tr: 火車五分鐘後開。

words.sent: Even a minute amount of the toxin can be dangerous.
words.tr: 即使極微量的毒素也可能有危險。

tip_zh: n. 分鐘（MIN-it）→ adj. 極微小的（my-NOOT）
tip_en: noun: sixty seconds; adjective: tiny, very detailed
trap: 拼法相同、讀音不同；SAT 常考 minute details／minute amounts。

name: muster

words.sent: The captain mustered the crew on deck for an emergency drill.
words.tr: 船長把船員召集到甲板上進行緊急演練。

words.def_: to summon up a feeling or quality
words.sent: She finally mustered the courage to ask her teacher for a recommendation letter.
words.tr: 她終於鼓起勇氣請老師寫推薦信。

tip_zh: 召集 → 鼓起（muster courage）；pass muster 合格
tip_en: to gather troops; to summon up a quality
trap: 學生把 muster 和 master 搞混，也不知道 muster courage 是「鼓起勇氣」。

name: patent

words.def_: a legal right to be the only maker of an invention
words.sent: The inventor received a patent for her improved water filter.
words.tr: 發明者為改良版濾水器取得專利。
words.src: Hot Words L48；字根字首 U115,116

words.sent: His excuse was a patent lie; everyone knew he had been at the game.
words.tr: 他的藉口顯然是謊言，大家都知道他去看比賽了。
words.src: Hot Words L48；字根字首 U115,116

tip_zh: n. 專利 → adj. 明顯的（patently false 顯然是錯的）
tip_en: noun: legal right to an invention; adjective: obvious
trap: SAT 中 patent／patently 常是「明顯」，與專利無關。

name: plastic

words.sent: Many cities have banned single-use plastic bags.
words.tr: 許多城市已禁用一次性塑膠袋。

words.sent: Children's brains are highly plastic, which helps them learn languages quickly.
words.tr: 兒童的大腦可塑性高，有助於快速學習語言。

tip_zh: n. 塑膠 → adj. 可塑的、易改變的（大腦的可塑性 plasticity）
tip_en: noun: synthetic material; adjective: easily shaped
trap: the brain is plastic 不是「大腦是塑膠」，而是「大腦可塑」。

name: poach

words.def_: to cook gently in simmering liquid
words.sent: The chef poached the eggs in water with a little vinegar.
words.tr: 主廚用加了少許醋的水煮荷包蛋。

words.def_: to hunt illegally; to take workers from a rival
words.sent: Rangers patrol the reserve day and night to stop people who poach elephants for ivory.
words.tr: 巡守員日夜巡邏保護區，阻止為象牙盜獵大象的人。

tip_zh: 水煮（蛋）→ 盜獵、挖角
tip_en: to cook gently in water; to hunt illegally or lure away
trap: SAT 中 poach 多指盜獵或挖角人才。

name: pore

words.def_: a tiny opening in the skin or a leaf
words.sent: Sweat leaves the body through millions of tiny pores.
words.tr: 汗水經由數百萬個小毛孔排出體外。

words.sent: The historian pored over old letters for months to reconstruct the family's story.
words.tr: 歷史學家花數月仔細研讀舊信件，以重建這家人的故事。

tip_zh: n. 毛孔 → v. pore over 仔細研讀
tip_en: noun: tiny skin opening; verb: to study closely
trap: pore over 常被誤寫成 pour over，也常被誤解為「毛孔」。

name: rail

words.sent: Hold the rail as you walk down the steep stairs.
words.tr: 走下陡梯時請抓好欄杆。

words.sent: Residents railed against the plan to build a highway through the park.
words.tr: 居民強烈抗議在公園中興建公路的計畫。

tip_zh: n. 欄杆、鐵軌 → v. rail against 怒斥
tip_en: noun: bar, track; verb: to complain bitterly
trap: rail against 和鐵路無關，是「強烈抱怨、抨擊」。

name: stem

words.def_: the main stalk of a plant
words.sent: Cut the flower stems at an angle so they absorb water better.
words.tr: 斜剪花莖，讓它們更容易吸水。

words.def_: (stem from) to originate; (stem) to stop the flow of
words.sent: Most of the arguments stem from a misunderstanding about who owns the land.
words.tr: 大部分爭執源自對土地歸屬的誤解。

tip_zh: n. 莖 → v. stem from 源自；stem the flow 遏止
tip_en: noun: plant stalk; verb: to originate; to stop
trap: SAT 同時考 stem from（源自）與 stem the tide（阻止），兩個意思方向相反。

name: yield

words.sent: The new rice variety yields twice as much grain per field.
words.tr: 這種新稻種每塊田的產量是原來的兩倍。

words.def_: to give way to pressure or force
words.sent: After weeks of protests, the government finally yielded to public pressure.
words.tr: 經過數週抗議，政府終於向民意讓步。

tip_zh: 產出 → 讓步、屈服（yield to pressure）；讓路
tip_en: to produce; to give way
trap: yield 在同一篇文章可能表示「產量」也可能是「屈服」，要看上下文。

name: betray

words.sent: The spy betrayed his country by selling secrets to the enemy.
words.tr: 間諜把機密賣給敵人，背叛了自己的國家。

words.sent: Although she claimed to be calm, her trembling hands betrayed her fear.
words.tr: 雖然她說自己很冷靜，發抖的雙手卻洩露了她的恐懼。

tip_zh: 背叛 → 無意中流露、洩露
tip_en: to be disloyal; to reveal unintentionally
trap: Her voice betrayed her nervousness 是「聲音透露出緊張」，不是背叛。

name: dispatch

words.def_: to send to a place for a purpose
words.sent: The city dispatched ambulances to the scene within minutes.
words.tr: 市府數分鐘內派遣救護車到現場。

words.sent: The clerk handled every complaint with dispatch, and the line soon disappeared.
words.tr: 店員迅速處理每件客訴，隊伍很快就消失了。

tip_zh: 派遣 → 迅速（with dispatch）；迅速處理掉
tip_en: to send off; speed and efficiency
trap: with dispatch 是「迅速地」，學生常看不懂。

name: forge

words.def_: to create something strong, such as a bond
words.sent: The two schools forged a partnership to share science equipment.
words.tr: 兩校建立合作關係，共享科學設備。

words.def_: to make an illegal copy of
words.sent: He was arrested for forging his employer's signature on checks.
words.tr: 他因在支票上偽造雇主簽名而被捕。

tip_zh: 鍛造 → 偽造（forgery）；forge ahead 穩步前進
tip_en: to shape metal; to fake; to advance steadily
trap: forge 同時可表示「打造關係」、「偽造」、「奮力前進」。

name: venture

words.sent: Their first business venture, a food truck, failed within a year.
words.tr: 他們第一次創業開餐車，一年內就失敗了。

words.sent: When no one answered, a shy student ventured a guess.
words.tr: 沒人回答時，一位害羞的學生大膽猜了一下。

tip_zh: n. 冒險事業 → v. 冒昧提出（venture an opinion/guess）
tip_en: noun: risky project; verb: to dare to say
trap: venture a guess 是「斗膽猜一下」，不是冒險旅行。

name: compass

words.sent: Without a compass, the hikers used the sun to find north.
words.tr: 沒有指南針，健行者靠太陽辨認北方。

words.sent: Questions about tax law fall outside the compass of this course.
words.tr: 稅法問題不在本課程的範圍內。

tip_zh: 指南針 → 範圍、界限（within the compass of）
tip_en: instrument for direction; range or scope
trap: SAT 中 compass 可指「範圍」，學生只知道指南針。

name: discount

words.sent: Students get a twenty percent discount at the museum.
words.tr: 學生在博物館可享八折優惠。

words.def_: to regard as unimportant or untrue
words.sent: Scientists once discounted the theory, but new evidence has revived it.
words.tr: 科學家曾不採信這個理論，但新證據讓它重獲重視。

tip_zh: 折扣 → v. 不予理會、不採信（discount a theory）
tip_en: reduction in price; to disregard
trap: discount the evidence 是「不採信證據」，不是「打折」。

name: checkered

words.sent: The café's checkered tablecloths give it a cheerful look.
words.tr: 咖啡館的格子桌巾讓它看起來很活潑。

words.def_: marked by periods of success and failure or wrongdoing
words.sent: Despite his checkered past, he was elected mayor by a wide margin.
words.tr: 儘管過去有不光彩的紀錄，他仍以大幅差距當選市長。

tip_zh: 格子花紋 → 時好時壞、有污點的（a checkered past）
tip_en: patterned in squares; marked by ups and downs
trap: a checkered career 不是「格子的職涯」，而是「起伏、有不光彩紀錄」。

name: pedestrian

words.sent: The new bridge has a separate lane for pedestrians and cyclists.
words.tr: 新橋設有行人和自行車專用道。
words.src: Hot Words L4；字根字首 U117

words.sent: Critics praised the actors but called the script pedestrian.
words.tr: 評論家稱讚演員，卻批評劇本平淡乏味。
words.src: Hot Words L4；字根字首 U117

tip_zh: n. 行人 → adj. 平淡乏味的（像走路一樣普通）
tip_en: noun: person walking; adjective: dull, ordinary
trap: SAT 常用 pedestrian 形容寫作「平庸無趣」。

name: sanction

words.sent: The school board sanctioned the new dress code after a public meeting.
words.tr: 學校委員會在公聽會後批准了新服裝規定。
words.src: Barron's U41；306/386 U25；VA U4；字根字首 U219

words.def_: a penalty for breaking a rule
words.sent: The United Nations imposed economic sanctions on the country.
words.tr: 聯合國對該國實施經濟制裁。
words.src: Barron's U41；306/386 U25；VA U4；字根字首 U219

tip_zh: 一字兩個相反意思：批准認可 ↔ 制裁懲罰
tip_en: to approve OR a penalty
trap: 學生只記一個意思，常把「批准」讀成「制裁」或反之。

name: cleave

words.sent: The axe cleaved the log in a single stroke.
words.tr: 斧頭一劈就把木頭劈成兩半。

words.sent: The village cleaves to traditions that have lasted for centuries.
words.tr: 這個村莊固守延續了數百年的傳統。

tip_zh: 一字兩個相反意思：劈開 ↔ 緊貼
tip_en: to split apart OR to cling to
trap: cleave 是「自反義詞」，cleave to tradition 是「堅守傳統」。

name: sustain

words.sent: The forest can sustain a large population of deer.
words.tr: 這片森林能維持大量鹿群生存。

words.def_: to suffer an injury or loss
words.sent: The driver sustained minor injuries in the crash.
words.tr: 駕駛在車禍中受了輕傷。

tip_zh: 維持 → 遭受（sustain injuries／losses）
tip_en: to keep going; to suffer
trap: sustain heavy damage 是「遭受嚴重損害」，不是「維持損害」。

name: catholic

words.def_: (Catholic) relating to the Roman Catholic Church
words.sent: The town's Catholic church was built in the twelfth century.
words.tr: 鎮上的天主教堂建於十二世紀。

words.def_: including a wide variety of things
words.sent: With catholic tastes in music, she listens to everything from opera to hip-hop.
words.tr: 她的音樂品味很廣，從歌劇到嘻哈都聽。

tip_zh: 大寫 Catholic 天主教 → 小寫 catholic 廣泛的、兼容並蓄的（catholic tastes）
tip_en: Catholic church; catholic = broad, universal
trap: SAT 中小寫 catholic 與宗教無關，指興趣「廣泛」。

name: provincial

words.sent: The provincial government manages schools and hospitals.
words.tr: 省政府管理學校和醫院。

words.sent: Traveling abroad challenged his provincial belief that his town did everything best.
words.tr: 出國旅行挑戰了他「家鄉什麼都最好」的狹隘想法。

tip_zh: 省的、地方的 → 眼界狹隘的、土氣的
tip_en: of a province; narrow-minded
trap: provincial attitudes 是「狹隘觀念」，不是行政區名稱。

name: clinical

words.def_: relating to the treatment of patients
words.sent: The drug is now in clinical trials with two thousand patients.
words.tr: 這款藥目前正對兩千名病患進行臨床試驗。

words.sent: She described the accident in a clinical voice, as if it had happened to someone else.
words.tr: 她用冷靜的語氣描述車禍，彷彿那是別人的事。

tip_zh: 臨床的 → 冷靜客觀、不帶感情的
tip_en: medical; coldly detached
trap: a clinical tone 是「冷冰冰、不帶感情的語氣」。

name: entrance

words.sent: The museum's main entrance is on the north side of the building.
words.tr: 博物館的主入口在建築北側。

words.def_: to fill with wonder and delight
words.sent: The dancers' graceful movements entranced the audience.
words.tr: 舞者優雅的動作讓觀眾看得入迷。

tip_zh: n. 入口（EN-trance）→ v. 使著迷（en-TRANCE，進入 trance 恍惚）
tip_en: noun: way in; verb: to fill with wonder
trap: 拼法相同，名詞與動詞重音、意思都不同。

name: warrant

words.def_: a legal document allowing police to act
words.sent: Police obtained a warrant to search the apartment.
words.tr: 警方取得搜索令搜查公寓。

words.sent: A small scratch does not warrant a trip to the emergency room.
words.tr: 小擦傷不值得去急診室。

tip_zh: n. 搜索令、逮捕令 → v. 使有正當理由（does not warrant）
tip_en: noun: legal document; verb: to justify
trap: The results warrant further study 是「結果值得進一步研究」。

name: qualify

words.def_: to meet the requirements for something
words.sent: Students with a B average qualify for the scholarship.
words.tr: 平均成績 B 以上的學生符合獎學金資格。

words.def_: to limit or modify a statement
words.sent: The author qualifies her claim, noting that the results apply only to large cities.
words.tr: 作者為她的主張加上限定，指出結果只適用於大城市。

tip_zh: 符合資格 → 限定、修飾（qualify a statement 加上但書）
tip_en: to meet requirements; to limit a statement
trap: SAT 閱讀題常問作者如何 qualify 一個主張，即「加上限制或但書」。

name: temper

words.sent: He lost his temper when the computer crashed for the third time.
words.tr: 電腦第三次當機時，他發起脾氣來。

words.sent: The teacher tempered her criticism with praise for the student's effort.
words.tr: 老師在批評中加入對學生努力的讚美，使語氣緩和。

tip_zh: n. 脾氣 → v. 緩和、調和（temper criticism with praise）
tip_en: noun: mood, anger; verb: to soften
trap: temper 作動詞是「使溫和」，SAT 常見。

name: appreciate

words.def_: to recognize the value of; to be grateful
words.sent: I really appreciate your help with the move.
words.tr: 很感謝你幫忙搬家。

words.sent: Land near the new station appreciated quickly after the train line opened.
words.tr: 鐵路通車後，新站附近的土地迅速增值。

tip_zh: 欣賞、感激 → 增值（反義 depreciate 貶值）
tip_en: to value or be grateful; to rise in value
trap: The house appreciated 是「房子增值」，不是房子懂得感恩。

name: arrest

words.def_: to take someone into police custody
words.sent: Police arrested two suspects outside the bank.
words.tr: 警方在銀行外逮捕兩名嫌犯。

words.sent: The new medicine can arrest the spread of the disease if given early.
words.tr: 若及早用藥，新藥能阻止疾病擴散。

tip_zh: 逮捕 → 阻止、抑制（arrest the spread）
tip_en: to seize by police; to stop a process
trap: arrest the decline 是「止住衰退」，與警察無關。

name: check

words.sent: Always check your answers before handing in the test.
words.tr: 交卷前一定要檢查答案。

words.sent: The constitution gives each branch of government power to check the others.
words.tr: 憲法賦予政府各部門彼此制衡的權力。

tip_zh: 檢查 → 抑制、遏止（checks and balances 制衡）
tip_en: to examine; to restrain
trap: SAT 常用 check 表示「制衡、抑制」。

name: wanting

words.sent: Wanting to save money, she cooked at home every night.
words.tr: 為了省錢，她每晚都在家煮飯。

words.sent: When the hurricane hit, the city's emergency plan was found wanting.
words.tr: 颶風來襲時，市府的緊急應變計畫被證明不足。

tip_zh: 想要 → adj. 欠缺的、不夠好的（found wanting 被發現不足）
tip_en: desiring; lacking, inadequate
trap: The plan was found wanting 是「計畫被認為不足」。

name: affect/effect

words.sent: Lack of sleep can affect your memory and mood.
words.tr: 睡眠不足會影響記憶和情緒。

words.sent: The new law had little effect on the number of accidents.
words.tr: 新法對事故數量幾乎沒有效果。

tip_zh: Affect 是 Action 動詞（影響）；Effect 是 End result 名詞（結果、效果）；effect 作動詞 = 造成（effect change）
tip_en: affect = verb (influence); effect = noun (result)
trap: 寫作和選擇題最常見的錯誤；effect 當動詞時意思是「實現、造成」，不是「影響」。

name: complement/compliment/complementary/complimentary

words.def_: to complete or go well with
words.sent: The spicy sauce complements the sweet flavor of the grilled fish.
words.tr: 辛辣醬汁和烤魚的甜味相得益彰。

words.sent: She blushed when the judge paid her a compliment on her performance.
words.tr: 評審稱讚她的表演時，她臉紅了。

words.def_: completing each other; going well together
words.sent: Blue and orange are complementary colors, so they stand out when placed side by side.
words.tr: 藍色和橘色是互補色，並排時特別醒目。
words.src: Hot Words L34；306/386 U5；字根字首 U12,121

words.sent: The hotel offers complimentary breakfast to every guest.
words.tr: 這家飯店為每位住客提供免費早餐。

tip_zh: complement 有 e = complete 使完整、互補；compliment 有 i = I like you 讚美；complementary 互補的；complimentary 免費贈送的、讚美的
tip_en: complement = complete; compliment = praise; complementary = completing each other; complimentary = free, praising
trap: 發音相同，寫作常拼錯；SAT 常考 complement 的「互補」。complimentary 除了「讚美的」，還常指「免費招待的」；complementary 則是「互補的」。

name: principal/principle

words.def_: most important; the head of a school
words.sent: The principal reason for the delay was a shortage of workers.
words.tr: 延誤的主要原因是人手不足。

words.sent: She refused the bribe because it went against her principles.
words.tr: 她拒絕賄賂，因為那違背她的原則。

tip_zh: principal 有 pal（夥伴）→ 校長、主要的；principle 結尾 -le 像 rule → 原則
tip_en: principal = main / head; principle = rule, belief
trap: 發音相同，寫作時極常混淆；principal 也可作形容詞「主要的」。

name: council/counsel/consul

words.def_: a group of people chosen to make decisions
words.sent: The city council voted to build a new library.
words.tr: 市議會投票決定興建新圖書館。

words.def_: advice; to give advice; a lawyer
words.sent: She sought counsel from her former teacher before choosing a university.
words.tr: 選大學前，她向以前的老師徵詢意見。

words.def_: a government official living in a foreign city to help citizens
words.sent: The consul in Osaka issued her a new passport within two days.
words.tr: 駐大阪領事兩天內就為她補發了新護照。

tip_zh: council 議會（cil 像 city 市議會）；counsel 建議、律師（sel 像 sell advice）；consul 領事（派駐外國城市的官員）
tip_en: council = group; counsel = advice / lawyer; consul = official in a foreign city
trap: 發音相同，寫作常混淆。council（議會）、counsel（建議／律師）、consul（領事）發音相近，寫作時常拼錯。

name: ensure/insure/assure

words.def_: to make certain that something happens
words.sent: Double-check the address to ensure the package arrives on time.
words.tr: 再次確認地址，以確保包裹準時送達。

words.sent: Most owners insure their homes against fire and flood.
words.tr: 多數屋主會為房屋投保火險與水險。

words.def_: to tell someone confidently to remove doubt
words.sent: The pilot assured passengers that the turbulence was not dangerous.
words.tr: 機長向乘客保證亂流並不危險。

tip_zh: ensure 確保（事情發生）；insure 投保；assure 向人保證（使人放心）
tip_en: ensure = make certain; insure = protect financially; assure = promise someone
trap: 三字都譯為「保證」，對象不同：ensure 事、insure 財產、assure 人。

name: imply/infer

words.sent: By checking his watch repeatedly, the host implied that it was time for the guests to leave.
words.tr: 主人頻頻看錶，暗示客人該離開了。

words.sent: From the wet streets, we inferred that it had rained during the night.
words.tr: 從潮濕的街道，我們推斷夜裡下過雨。

tip_zh: 說話的人 imply（暗示，送出訊息）；聽的人 infer（推論，接收訊息）
tip_en: speaker implies; listener infers
trap: 學生常把 infer 當成 imply；SAT 閱讀題「It can be inferred」就是讀者推論。

name: comprise/compose/constitute

words.sent: The committee comprises twelve members from different departments.
words.tr: 委員會由十二位來自不同部門的成員組成。

words.def_: to make up a whole; to create music or writing
words.sent: Small family farms compose most of the region's agriculture.
words.tr: 小型家庭農場構成該地區大部分的農業。

words.def_: to make up or form a whole
words.sent: Women constitute more than half of the university's students.
words.tr: 女性占這所大學學生的一半以上。

tip_zh: 整體 comprises 部分（包含）；部分 compose 整體（組成）；is comprised of 為常見誤用；constitute 構成（部分 constitute 整體，用法同 compose）
tip_en: the whole comprises the parts; the parts compose the whole; constitute = make up
trap: SAT 文法題會考主詞方向：The team comprises ten players／Ten players compose the team。部分 compose／constitute 整體；整體 comprises 部分，方向別搞反。

name: discreet/discrete/discretion

words.def_: careful not to attract attention or reveal secrets
words.sent: Please be discreet; no one else knows about the surprise party.
words.tr: 請低調一點，其他人都不知道這場驚喜派對。
words.src: Barron's U33；Hot Words L22；306/386 U9；字根字首 U22

words.sent: The project was divided into five discrete stages, each with its own deadline.
words.tr: 這項計畫分成五個獨立階段，各有截止日。

words.def_: the freedom to decide; the quality of being careful about what one says
words.sent: Teachers may use their discretion in deciding whether to accept late work.
words.tr: 老師可自行決定是否接受遲交的作業。

tip_zh: discreet 謹慎低調（ee 兩個眼睛默默看）；discrete 分離的（t 把兩個 e 隔開）；discretion 自行決定權；謹慎（discreet 的名詞）
tip_en: discreet = careful, tactful; discrete = separate; discretion = freedom to decide; tact
trap: 發音相同；discrete 常出現在科學文章（discrete units）。discretion 是 discreet 的名詞，不是 discrete（分離的）的名詞。

name: averse/adverse/adversity

words.sent: She is averse to taking risks with her savings.
words.tr: 她不願拿積蓄冒險。

words.sent: The drug was withdrawn after reports of adverse side effects.
words.tr: 有不良副作用的報告後，該藥被下架。

words.sent: She showed great courage in the face of adversity after losing her home in the flood.
words.tr: 洪水奪走她的家後，她在逆境中展現了極大的勇氣。
words.src: Hot Words L10,69；字根字首 U3,146

tip_zh: averse 人「反感、不願意」（averse to risk）；adverse 事情「不利的」（adverse effects）；adversity 逆境（adverse 不利的 → 名詞）
tip_en: averse = unwilling (people); adverse = harmful (things); adversity = hardship
trap: 只差 d，SAT 常考兩者的搭配對象。adversity 是 adverse 的名詞；averse 的名詞則是 aversion（反感）。

name: continual/continuous

words.sent: The continual interruptions from phone calls made it hard to finish the report.
words.tr: 電話一再打斷，讓報告難以完成。
words.src: Hot Words L60；字根字首 U15,137

words.sent: The machine can run for forty-eight hours of continuous operation.
words.tr: 這台機器可連續運轉四十八小時。
words.src: Hot Words L60；字根字首 U15,137

tip_zh: continual 反覆、斷斷續續地發生；continuous 不間斷、連續不停
tip_en: continual = repeated; continuous = unbroken
trap: 兩者都譯為「持續」，但 continual 中間有停頓，continuous 沒有。

name: explicit/implicit/explicate

words.sent: The instructions were explicit: no phones in the exam room.
words.tr: 規定很明確：考場內不得有手機。

words.sent: Her silence contained an implicit criticism of the plan.
words.tr: 她的沉默隱含對計畫的批評。

words.sent: The professor spent an entire class explicating a single poem.
words.tr: 教授花了整堂課詳細解說一首詩。
words.src: Hot Words L90；VA U39；字根字首 U28

tip_zh: explicit 明確說出的（ex- 向外講出來）；implicit 隱含的（im- 藏在裡面）；explicate 詳細解釋（ex- 打開 + plic 摺 → 把摺起來的展開）
tip_en: explicit = stated clearly; implicit = implied; explicate = explain in detail
trap: SAT 閱讀題常問作者 explicitly 或 implicitly 表達了什麼。explicate、explicit、implicit 同字根 plic（摺）：攤開說明 vs 摺在裡面。

name: elicit/illicit/solicit

words.sent: The teacher's question elicited a lively discussion.
words.tr: 老師的問題引發熱烈討論。

words.sent: Customs officers discovered an illicit shipment of rare birds.
words.tr: 海關人員查獲一批非法走私的稀有鳥類。

words.sent: The museum is soliciting donations to repair its roof.
words.tr: 博物館正在募款修繕屋頂。

tip_zh: elicit 引出（e- 向外拉出回應）；illicit 違法的（il- = illegal）；solicit 請求、徵求（donations, opinions）
tip_en: elicit = draw out; illicit = illegal; solicit = ask for
trap: 發音相近，詞性不同：elicit 動詞，illicit 形容詞。elicit（引出回應）、solicit（主動請求）、illicit（違法）三字都以 -licit 結尾。

name: precede/proceed/precedent

words.def_: to come before in time or order
words.sent: A short film will precede the main feature.
words.tr: 正片放映前會先播一部短片。

words.sent: After the fire alarm ended, the exam proceeded as planned.
words.tr: 火災警報結束後，考試照原定計畫進行。

words.def_: an earlier event used as an example for later ones
words.sent: The court's decision set a precedent for similar cases in the future.
words.tr: 法院的判決為日後類似案件立下先例。

tip_zh: precede 在…之前（pre- 前面）；proceed 繼續進行（pro- 向前走）；precedent 先例（n.，precede 在前）
tip_en: precede = come before; proceed = go forward; precedent = earlier example
trap: 拼法相近，寫作常把 proceed 寫成 procede。precedent 是名詞，拼法跟 precede 一樣是 -cede-，不是 proceed 的 -ceed。

name: evoke/invoke/provoke/revoke

words.def_: to bring a feeling or memory to mind
words.sent: The smell of baking bread evoked memories of her grandmother's kitchen.
words.tr: 烤麵包的香味喚起她對祖母廚房的回憶。

words.def_: to cite as an authority; to call upon
words.sent: The lawyer invoked a 1964 ruling to support her argument.
words.tr: 律師援引 1964 年的判決支持她的論點。

words.def_: to cause a strong reaction, especially anger
words.sent: The referee's unfair call provoked angry shouts from the fans.
words.tr: 裁判不公的判決引來球迷憤怒的叫喊。

words.sent: The city revoked the restaurant's license after it failed three health inspections.
words.tr: 這家餐廳三次未通過衛生檢查後，市府吊銷了它的執照。

tip_zh: evoke 喚起（回憶、感覺，e- 引出來）；invoke 援引（法律、權威）、祈求（in- 呼喚進來）；provoke 激怒、引起（pro- 向前叫出）；revoke 撤銷（re- 叫回來）
tip_en: evoke = bring to mind; invoke = cite, appeal to; provoke = cause anger; revoke = cancel
trap: 兩字都譯「喚起／召喚」，但 evoke 對象是感受，invoke 對象是規則或權威。四字都是 -voke（叫喚），差在字首：e- 叫出感覺、in- 叫來權威、pro- 挑起反應、re- 收回。

name: hoard/horde

words.def_: to collect and hide a large supply
words.sent: Before the storm, some shoppers hoarded bottled water and batteries.
words.tr: 暴風雨前，一些購物者囤積瓶裝水和電池。
words.src: Barron's U25；Hot Words L9；306/386 U13；字根字首 U191

words.sent: Hordes of tourists crowded into the square to see the parade.
words.tr: 成群遊客擠進廣場觀看遊行。

tip_zh: hoard 囤積（hoard 有 a = amass 累積）；horde 一大群（horde 有 e = everyone 一群人）
tip_en: hoard = store up; horde = crowd
trap: 發音相同，寫作常拼錯。

name: fortuitous/fortunate

words.sent: Their meeting was fortuitous; both had missed the same train.
words.tr: 他們的相遇純屬偶然，兩人都錯過了同一班火車。
words.src: Barron's U12；Hot Words L68；306/386 U12；字根字首 U185

words.sent: We were fortunate to find seats on such a crowded train.
words.tr: 在那麼擁擠的火車上找到座位，我們真幸運。
words.src: Hot Words L68；字根字首 U185

tip_zh: fortuitous 偶然的（fortuit 出於偶然，不一定是好事）；fortunate 幸運的
tip_en: fortuitous = by chance; fortunate = lucky
trap: 常被誤用為「幸運的」，SAT 嚴格用法是「偶然、碰巧」。

name: perpetrate/perpetuate/perpetual

words.sent: Investigators are still searching for the people who perpetrated the fraud.
words.tr: 調查人員仍在追查犯下這起詐欺的人。

words.sent: Cartoons that show scientists as old men perpetuate a narrow stereotype.
words.tr: 把科學家畫成老先生的卡通延續了狹隘的刻板印象。

words.sent: The city seems to be in a perpetual state of construction.
words.tr: 這座城市似乎永遠在施工。
words.src: Hot Words L60；306/386 U21；字根字首 U57

tip_zh: perpetrate 犯下（壞事，perpetrator 犯人）；perpetuate 使延續（perpetual 永久的）；perpetual 永久的（perpetuate 的形容詞）
tip_en: perpetrate = commit a crime; perpetuate = make last; perpetual = never ending
trap: 字形相近，perpetuate stereotypes 是「延續刻板印象」。perpetual 和 perpetuate 一家，都是「延續」；perpetrate 則是犯罪。

name: persecute/prosecute

words.def_: to treat cruelly because of beliefs or identity
words.sent: The regime persecuted journalists who criticized the government.
words.tr: 這個政權迫害批評政府的記者。

words.sent: The state decided to prosecute the company for polluting the river.
words.tr: 州政府決定起訴這家公司污染河川。

tip_zh: persecute 迫害（因種族宗教等）；prosecute 起訴（pro- 在法庭上提出）
tip_en: persecute = oppress; prosecute = take legal action
trap: 只差 er／ro，一個是不公義的迫害，一個是合法的訴訟。

name: loath/loathe/loathsome

words.sent: The mayor was loath to raise taxes during an election year.
words.tr: 市長在選舉年不願加稅。

words.sent: Many students loathe group projects in which one person does all the work.
words.tr: 很多學生討厭一人包辦全部工作的分組報告。

words.sent: The villain in the story is a loathsome man who cheats orphans out of their money.
words.tr: 故事裡的反派是個騙取孤兒錢財的可惡之人。
words.src: Hot Words L74；字根字首 U197

tip_zh: loath（adj.）不情願的；loathe（v.）厭惡，多一個 e 動詞要「動」；loathsome 令人厭惡的（loathe 的形容詞）
tip_en: loath = unwilling; loathe = hate; loathsome = disgusting
trap: 只差一個 e，詞性和意思不同。loathsome 來自 loathe（厭惡），loath 卻是「不情願的」。

name: allude/elude/delude

words.sent: The speaker alluded to recent scandals without naming anyone.
words.tr: 講者暗指最近的醜聞，卻沒點名任何人。
words.src: Barron's U41；306/386 U2；VA U8；字根字首 U3

words.def_: to escape from; to fail to be understood
words.sent: The thief eluded police for three weeks.
words.tr: 小偷躲避警方追捕長達三週。

words.def_: to make someone believe something false
words.sent: Don't delude yourself into thinking the test will be easy.
words.tr: 別自欺欺人以為考試會很簡單。
words.src: Barron's U22；Hot Words L36；字根字首 U19

tip_zh: allude 間接提及（al- 指向）；elude 逃避、難以理解（e- 溜出去）；delude 欺騙（delusion 的動詞）
tip_en: allude = refer indirectly; elude = escape; delude = deceive
trap: 發音相近；allude to 後接被提到的事物。三字都是 -lude（玩），al- 暗指、e- 逃脫、de- 欺騙。

name: prescribe/proscribe/ascribe

words.def_: to recommend a medicine or course of action
words.sent: The doctor prescribed rest and plenty of fluids.
words.tr: 醫師囑咐多休息、多喝水。

words.sent: The new law proscribes smoking in all public buildings.
words.tr: 新法禁止在所有公共建築內吸菸。

words.def_: to say that something is caused by or belongs to someone
words.sent: Historians ascribe the empire's fall to a series of poor harvests.
words.tr: 歷史學家把帝國的衰亡歸因於連年歉收。

tip_zh: prescribe 開藥方、規定（pre- 事先寫好）；proscribe 禁止（pro- 公告出去禁止）；ascribe 歸因於（ascribe A to B）
tip_en: prescribe = recommend, order; proscribe = forbid; ascribe = attribute
trap: 只差一個字母，意思幾乎相反。三字都是 -scribe（寫），ascribe 是「寫在某人帳上 → 歸因」。

name: emigrate/immigrate/migrate

words.def_: to leave one's country to live in another
words.sent: Her grandparents emigrated from Italy in 1950.
words.tr: 她的祖父母於 1950 年從義大利移民出去。

words.def_: to come to live permanently in a new country
words.sent: Many families immigrated to Canada in search of better jobs.
words.tr: 許多家庭移民到加拿大尋找更好的工作。

words.def_: to move from one place to another, often with the seasons
words.sent: Every autumn, millions of birds migrate south to warmer regions.
words.tr: 每年秋天，數百萬隻鳥向南遷徙到溫暖的地區。

tip_zh: emigrate 移出（e- = exit 離開母國）；immigrate 移入（im- = into 進入新國家）；migrate 遷徙（不強調出或入，動物也可用）
tip_en: emigrate from; immigrate to; migrate = move from place to place
trap: 學生常不清楚哪個搭配 from、哪個搭配 to。migrate 是總稱，emigrate 強調「移出」、immigrate 強調「移入」。

name: militate/mitigate/litigate

words.def_: (militate against) to be a powerful factor preventing
words.sent: The high cost of land militates against building new parks downtown.
words.tr: 高昂地價不利於在市中心興建新公園。

words.sent: Planting trees along the river can mitigate the effects of flooding.
words.tr: 沿河植樹可減輕洪水的影響。
words.src: Hot Words L5；306/386 U18；字根字首 U85,113

words.def_: to take a dispute to a court of law
words.sent: Rather than litigate for years, the two companies agreed to settle the dispute privately.
words.tr: 兩家公司不想打好幾年官司，同意私下和解。

tip_zh: militate 起作用（militate against 不利於）；mitigate 減輕（mitigate the damage）；litigate 打官司（lit 爭論）
tip_en: militate = work against; mitigate = lessen; litigate = go to court
trap: 常被誤用成 mitigate against；正確是 militate against。三字只差一兩個字母：militate 起作用、mitigate 減輕、litigate 訴訟。

name: denote/connote

words.def_: to be a sign of; to mean literally
words.sent: On this map, red dots denote hospitals.
words.tr: 地圖上的紅點代表醫院。

words.def_: to suggest an idea in addition to the literal meaning
words.sent: "Home" connotes warmth and safety, while "house" simply names a building.
words.tr: 「家」隱含溫暖與安全，「房子」只是指一棟建築。

tip_zh: denote 字面意思（de- 直接標記）；connote 言外之意、聯想（con- 一起帶出的感覺）
tip_en: denote = literal meaning; connote = suggested associations
trap: SAT 閱讀題常問用字的 connotation（言外之意）。

name: disburse/disperse/dispense

words.def_: to pay out money from a fund
words.sent: The foundation will disburse the grants to schools in March.
words.tr: 基金會將於三月撥款給各校。

words.sent: Police used loudspeakers to disperse the crowd after the concert.
words.tr: 演唱會後警方用擴音器疏散人群。

words.def_: to give out; (dispense with) to do without
words.sent: The machine dispenses free water to anyone with a reusable bottle.
words.tr: 這台機器為帶環保瓶的人免費供水。

tip_zh: disburse 支付（burse = purse 錢包）；disperse 驅散、散開（spers 散）；dispense 分發（藥、水等）；dispense with 省去
tip_en: disburse = pay out; disperse = scatter; dispense = give out
trap: 發音相近，一個關於錢，一個關於散開。disburse 發錢、disperse 散開、dispense 分發物品，三字都以 dis- 開頭、長得很像。

name: tortuous/torturous

words.def_: full of twists and turns; overly complicated
words.sent: The tortuous mountain road had more than forty sharp turns.
words.tr: 這條曲折的山路有四十多個急彎。

words.sent: The last kilometer of the marathon was torturous for the injured runner.
words.tr: 馬拉松最後一公里對受傷的跑者來說是一大折磨。

tip_zh: tortuous 曲折的（tort 扭，路彎彎曲曲）；torturous 痛苦折磨的（torture）
tip_en: tortuous = twisting; torturous = painful
trap: 兩字只差一個 r，學生常以為都是「痛苦」。

name: flaunt/flout

words.sent: He flaunted his new sports car by driving it slowly past his old school.
words.tr: 他開著新跑車慢慢經過母校炫耀。

words.sent: Drivers who flout the speed limit near schools face heavy fines.
words.tr: 在學校附近無視速限的駕駛將面臨重罰。
words.src: Barron's U7；Hot Words L80；字根字首 U185

tip_zh: flaunt 炫耀（a 像 admire me）；flout 公然藐視（o 像 out of the rules）
tip_en: flaunt = show off; flout = openly disobey
trap: 母語人士也常把 flout the rules 誤寫成 flaunt the rules。

name: appraise/apprise

words.def_: to assess the value or quality of
words.sent: An expert was hired to appraise the antique clock.
words.tr: 聘請專家為古董鐘估價。

words.sent: Please apprise me of any changes to the schedule.
words.tr: 行程如有變動請通知我。
words.src: Hot Words L90；字根字首 U162

tip_zh: appraise 估價、評估（praise 價值）；apprise 通知、告知（apprise sb of sth）
tip_en: appraise = evaluate; apprise = inform
trap: 只差一個 a；apprise 常被誤寫成 appraise。

name: exalt/exult

words.def_: to praise highly; to raise in rank
words.sent: The poem exalts the courage of ordinary people during the war.
words.tr: 這首詩讚頌戰爭期間平凡人的勇氣。
words.src: Hot Words L19,79；字根字首 U27

words.sent: Fans exulted in the streets after their team won the championship.
words.tr: 球隊奪冠後，球迷在街頭狂歡。
words.src: Barron's U17；Hot Words L19；字根字首 U29

tip_zh: exalt 讚揚、提升地位（alt = high）；exult 狂喜歡騰（ult 像 ultimate joy）
tip_en: exalt = praise highly; exult = rejoice
trap: 只差一個母音，閱讀時常混淆。

name: forbear/forebear

words.sent: She forbore from commenting on her friend's strange haircut.
words.tr: 她忍住沒評論朋友奇怪的髮型。

words.sent: Our forebears farmed this valley for more than three hundred years.
words.tr: 我們的祖先在這座山谷務農了三百多年。

tip_zh: forbear（v.）克制、忍住；forebear（n.）祖先（fore- 前面的人）
tip_en: forbear = refrain; forebear = ancestor
trap: 只差一個 e，詞性與意思都不同。
